title: Ensure cell broadcast alerts cannot be easily muted
description:
Currently cell broadcast messages can fail to produce feedbackd alert sounds in at least two ways:
 
 1. Phosh sends the alert event to feedbackd with its `mobi.phosh.Shell` app-id. The same app-id profile is also used for shell feedback events like haptics on window closing etc. and the user may have set the profile to 'silent' to avoid these. The silent profile also silences the cell broadcast alerts.
 2. The main volume may be set to zero causing the feedbackd alert to be silent.

If I've understood correctly, using cellbroadcastd directly (#1315) could help with having separate app-ids for shell feedback events and cell broacast messages.

As for the zero volume problem, the feedbackd interface could perhaps gain a new 'alert' hint, which would override a low volume setting with a higher one. The volume override should probably be opt-in with a configurable override volume level.

title: cellbroadcast: Use cellbroadcastd
description:
Once cellbroadcastd grows a [monitor mode](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/devrtz/cellbroadcastd/-/merge_requests/40) we want to pull messages from it (rather than listening to MM) as cbd then becomes the only source of truth, allowing it to delete the messages from MM after reception.

This avoids the CBM showing up multiple times when the user e.g. logs back in without MM restarting.

description:

* [ ] When pulling up the bottom bar we have some flicker as the overviews background starts to alpha blend just a little bit before bringing up the thumb. We want to get them in sync (don't start the toplevel's background blend before the thumbnail-overlay is mapped).
* [x] When launching an app from the app-grid we show the thumbnail-overlay that then fights with the launch splash. !1950 helps here and we could also look into !1264 while at that.

title: Make orientation setting persist across restarts and when between sensor being available / unavailable
description:
Environment: phosh/phoc v0.25.2, pureos10, Librem 5, Mobile Phone.

Maybe related to issue #754

Steps to repeat:

1. open quick settings panel swiping down
2. make sure the HKS switch is on (device power off) for wifi, camera/microphone, so only wwan 4G is running,
3. long press orientation to switch it to manual showing "Portrait"
4. turn HKS on for wwan powering down the modem,
5. this activates L5 lockdown mode which turns off the auto rotate sensor and changes the quicksetting for screen rotate to "Off",
6. turn off the HKS which powers on the wwan modem, 
5. Observe once 4G is back up and connected the Orientation quick setting still shows "Off"

What it should be showing is last used setting which could be either "Off", "Portrait/Landscape", or "On" for autorotate. In the above example it should switch to Portrait manual.

![persistentOrientation](/uploads/824d407cecc9f750358acb22ba6ede90/persistentOrientation.png)

![persistentorientation2](/uploads/4dac868efa0fab280729248c574ab8bd/persistentorientation2.png)

This story could be expanded or used to build automated test cases to make sure all quick settings are presistent especially after power cycling, phone restart, phone running out of battery completely, exiting lockdown mode, after resume from suspend, or when phosh shell crashes and restarts. Did not test other quicksettings to see if issues such as this one exist.

Additional Tests done:
Test2
Setup: wwan power off, wifi power off, camera/microphone power on, rotation on portrait manual, rotation sensor on.
Observation: when switching on HKS for camera powering off the camera/microphone the L5 is entering lockdown mode, however the rotation quicksetting button does not switch from portrait manual to "Off" indicating the sensor may still be on, while it is not,.

In this case the user can still manually rotate the screen in lockdown mode (which is desirable).

description:
In PostmarketOS (and maybe also other OS's?) one can set the mode of the USB device (to charging only, developer mode, mass storage etc.) with [usb-signaller](https://codeberg.org/DylanVanAssche/usb-signaller).

Currently the UI for mode setting uses notifications. This does not work too well, since notifications allow only 3 buttons and there are at least 4 mode choices in normal devices. It's also easy to dismiss the notification and there is no obvious way to get it to appear again.

A quick setting would be an obvious place to set the USB mode and would improve the user experience with this feature.

title: app-tracker: Better monitor app startup
description:
There's several things we can do to better track app startup so we don't notify the user about apps that would start up eventually:

- [x] flatpak scope matching (see below)
- [x] monitor when the DBus name is taken (https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/merge_requests/1915#note_2790229)
- [ ] Allowing the user to hide the notification for this app (we have the app-id and could add a "don't show again" button).

## flatpak

Similar to !1915 we can monitor flatpak startup by looking at the

```
Sender=:1.1  Path=/org/freedesktop/systemd1  Interface=org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager  Member=JobRemoved
```

signal and match that on the started app-id e.g. `app-flatpak-org.gnome.design.IconLibrary-3821766977.scope`. If we see that the command at least started and we can give it more startup time / track it.

title: Lockscreen lock slow with glycin loaders
description:
The switch to glycin in gdkpixbuf made screen locking on devices with slower I/O (e.g. the Pixel 3A) pretty slow. The first second after hitting the lock button shows `glycin-loaders` eating up all CPU.

I don't think there's an easy way around this so we likely need to cache the surface and keep it around rather than creating it on lock. This has consequences for lockscreen plugins that now can't now create state anymore on lock but need to keep it around (e.g. the ticketbox plugin needs a file monitor now (#896)).

title: Brightness slider too wide without autobrightness
description: If we have brightness but no autobrightness (and thus the button to unfold the autobrightness toggle is hidden) the slider is too wide as it can be pulled to the very right screen edge so there's some missing right margin.

## What is the expected behaviour?

title: Feature Request: Add a Rotate Button in Phosh Mobile Shell
description:
**Feature Description**

A rotate button should appear in the bottom corner of the screen whenever the device detects a rotation. This button would provide users the option to manually confirm or deny the screen orientation change, offering better control over the device’s behaviour in scenarios where automatic rotation may not be desired.

Example found in android phones

![image](/uploads/15276776dfdebac6cbade4c18ba008f9/image.png)

**Proposed Design**

- Trigger: The button appears whenever the device detects a change in orientation (e.g., from portrait to landscape).
- Placement: Positioned in the bottom-right or bottom-left corner of the screen for easy access without interfering with other UI elements.
- Appearance: A small, unobtrusive icon representing rotation, such as a curved arrow or screen outline.
- Behavior: The button fades away after 3-5 seconds if no interaction occurs. Tapping the button confirms the rotation, while ignoring it keeps the current orientation.

**Optional Enhancements**

- Settings Toggle: Add an option in the settings to enable or disable this feature.

title: Delay in moving keyboard focus from app to search
description:
With a hardware keyboard in desktop/docked mode the overview is shown by pressing the 'Super' key. The keyboard input is then directed to the search box, but there is a small delay after pressing Super when the keyboard input is still sent to the currently open app.

On my setup this delay is about 200 ms, enough for at least the first character of the search string to be sent to the open app, if one starts typing immediately after pressing Super. This not only causes the search to fail, but also sends wrong input to the app, which may in some apps (with vim-style keys) cause Bad Things to happen.

title: Rework PhoshActivity and PhoshOverview
description:
Currently `PhoshOverview` manually manages the relationship between `PhoshToplevel` (a representation of wlr-foreign-toplevel) and `PhoshActivity` (a display-only widget with an activity card), by tracking them with `g_object_{set/get}_data}`, requesting and passing window thumbnails etc.

This is far from ideal - `PhoshOverview` is already quite a messy thing having multiple responsibilities. However, the most obvious way of fixing that - letting `PhoshActivity` consume and handle `PhoshToplevel` by itself - isn't good either, since 1:1 relationship between `PhoshActivity` and `PhoshToplevel` is very temporary (see #324; and potentially other things in the future like splash screens or suspended activites).

We need a new entity responsible for representing and managing a single activity. I'd propose renaming current `PhoshActivity` into `PhoshActivityCard`, and creating a new `PhoshActivity` class that would then handle any actual logic by itself, allowing `PhoshOverview` to not care about activity implementation details.

This way, `PhoshActivityCard` could just represent the state of any `PhoshActivity` given to it, regardless of its internal implementation, freeing `PhoshOverview` from unwanted responsibilities. This also opens a path for compositing multiple thumbnails onto a single activity, as needed for window stacks (#324), without cluttering classes that shouldn't need to care about it, since this whole logic could be then properly contained in implementation of `PhoshActivity`.

This may also touch `PhoshThumbnail`, since currently it sits in a rather awkward place between Overview, Toplevel and Activity.

title: Improve docs and build enviroment
description:
This issue is a proposal to improve documentation  
with the intention of improving build instructions  
and onboarding experience for newcomers.

## Why this proposal exists?

When developing multiple projects simultaneously
or using an old distribution for development  
it is relatively easy to end up with conflicting
or missing versions of build dependencies.

Anecdotally exactly this scenario has happened recently,
when a couple of people on [#phosh@talk.puri.sm][1]  
had an issue building the current development version
of _phosh_ on their *stable* Debian distributions.

## What this proposal wants to achieve?

In order to minimise the friction with setting up
the build environment it is proposed to utilize  
containers to manage build dependencies provisioning.

## How this proposal wants to do it?

Some preliminary work has been done to improve
the building instructions in [KacperS/phosh/docs/building.md][2].  
At first the building instructions were supposed to contain
snippets to create containers with needed build dependencies.  
But after some consideration it has been concluded, that
those snippets should be integrated into `.gitlab-ci.yml`  
in order to make sure that the build instructions aren't outdated.
Moreover in order to improve the brevity of documentation  
it would be beneficial to separate said snippets into
self contained tool akin to what `gnome-shell` [uses][3],  
which also provides integration with [GNOME Builder][4].

## Roadmap

1. [ ] Create a tool for development inside toolbox images
    1. [ ] Creating toolbox containers with build dependencies
    2. [ ] Copying/Mounting glib schemas into container
    3. [ ] Configuring $DISPLAY and other variables  
           to run a nested _phosh_ session inside the toolbox
2. [ ] Integrating build environment containers into CI/CD
3. [ ] Better integration with GNOME Builder through `.buildconfig`
4. [ ] (Optional) Use [jhbuild][5]

## Post scriptum

I hope that I've argument my point of view clearly
and I also hope that the `proposal` does not read as a `demand`.  
Nota bene knowing how open source developers are underappreciated
I also want to thank anyone who contributed to this project :heart:.

## Post post scriptum

If this proposal is rejected, would changes to build instructions
presented in [KacperS/phosh/docs/building.md][2] still be welcomed
(without the container bits ofc) ?

[1]: matrix:#phosh@talk.puri.sm
[2]: https://gitlab.gnome.org/KacperS/phosh/-/blob/improve_docs/docs/building.md
[3]: https://github.com/gnomegit1/-gnome-shell/tree/main/tools/toolbox
[4]: https://apps.gnome.org/Builder/
[5]: https://gitlab.com/GNOME/jhbuilb

title: Fingerprint activity indicator
description:
I'm using [`phrog`](https://github.com/samcday/phrog) with greetd as the greeter (instead of GDM) on my Framework laptop.

Once I enrolled my fingerprints via `gnome-control-center`, it seems that the default greetd / system (Fedora Silverblue) PAM stack was updated to allow fingerprint logins.

As a result, I can already do a fingerprint login to my laptop from cold boot with phosh:

![1000000218-cut-merged-1717659737789](/uploads/81cd8753904f0f1c4d533ce7f168d1c5/1000000218-cut-merged-1717659737789.mp4)

As the video demonstrates, phrog has displayed the "please present a fingerprint" message that percolated through the PAM stack. Once the fingerprint was presented, the PAM/greetd conversation progressed to a newly created session.

I understand that the primary devices Phosh is targeting today do not feature biometrics login devices like this. I assume though, at some point there will be such devices on the market? And I am indeed daily driving phosh on my laptop as the greeter (via phrog).

So, it would be cool if Phosh had more fingerprint support.

When I do a fingerprint thing, I confirmed via `busctl monitor` that lots of interesting stuff is happening via the [`net.reactivated.Fprint`](https://fprint.freedesktop.org/fprintd-dev/) system D-Bus API.

In particular, I observed the `finger-needed` property changing to `true` during a fingerprint auth prompt. What if we, as a start, displayed the [fingerprint icon](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/adwaita-icon-theme/-/blob/master/Adwaita/symbolic/devices/auth-fingerprint-symbolic.svg) in the top panel whenever the system bus indicates that an imminent fingerprint scan is expected?

title: Allow top-panel power menu to be displayed on custom lockscreens
description:
https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/merge_requests/1055 explicitly hides the power menu on the lockscreen.

As Guido explains in the comments below, this was intentional as the overlay that is displayed when the physical power button is long-pressed is more appropriate for these actions.

However, an unlocked phosh-session *does* show the power menu in the top right of the top-panel. I think the phrog interactions should match *this*, rather than the lockscreen of an active phosh-session.

As such, this issue is requesting a way to allow custom lockscreens / phrog to be able to force the top-panel power menu to be displayed.

title: Allow shutdown button in power menu to be enabled on lockscreens
description:
This would be generally useful (see #414), but it essential for :frog: - it needs to be possible for users to easily shutdown their device before they've spawned a logged-in phosh-session.

So at the very least, libphosh consumers like phrog need to be able to force the enablement of these power menu actions, regardless of any security/data-integrity concerns. This is because greetd is not a multi-session capable greeter like GDM, so when you're looking at phrog, you're sure that no users are currently logged in (of course, if this ever changed in future phrog would have the same concerns as phosh-session in terms of protecting data integrity)

title: Support light theme
description:
Being outdoors in brighter sun, it is somewhat common for me to be unable to lock the phone in any way other than 99% blindly because I can't really see anything. The PinePhone in particular just doesn't have a screen that is bright enough for these conditions (might be less of an issue with the Librem 5). Once the device is unlocked however, things tend to be mostly fine - because I use all apps on my phone with black text on white bg so they're all super bright, which somehow also makes the text just about readable under most conditions where dark mode-alikes fail. I'm not sure why exactly it is like that, but it seems like white on dark like the lock screen is just inherently way less usable under direct light.

Therefore, I'm suggesting that the settings have an easy toggle to make the lockscreen (both the clock view when not scrolled up to the PIN unlock part, and the PIN keyboard itself) a bright white with black text & elements, so the exact opposite to what it is now. I would suggest to not tie this to the notification bar color when unlocked and general app dark mode or anything else, since this is only really a usability issue for me on the lock screen anyway, and I feel like that might also be the case for others.

I don't care if it's the default, the current black certainly looks sleek and I'm sure a lot of people are fine with it. But those who find the sunlight issues a bit too much to deal with, might be worth a toggle.

title: Lockscreen: always return to main unlock screen after blanking screen
description:
When the screen is blanked (being turning off) while the lockscreen is active, the state of the lockscreen is preserved when turning on the screen again instead of returning to the main lockscreen page.

Steps to reproduce:

1. press power button to blank screen and lock
2. press power button to show lockscreen
3. swipe down to show top bar
4. press power button to blank screen again
5. press power button to show lockscreen again

Actual result: the top bar is still pulled down

Expected result: the main page of the lockscreen (with the clock and "swipe up to unlock") is shown

This also affects lock screen widget pages.

In my view the common expectation is that blanking the screen always returns the UI to a well-known state.

title: Make the lockscreen adaptive/work in landscape orientation
description:
Currently the lockscreen is portrait-only, meaning if the user selects the landscape orientation, phosh changes the display orientation when locking and unlocking the screen.

This is counter-intuitive and introduces unnecessary complexity in the lockscreen code (need to save current transform, switch to portrait, then re-apply transform when unlocking).

Having the lockscreen work in landscape orientation would require a landscape mode design so it can fit in 360px height (cc @tobias.bernard ), probably by putting blocks side-by-side. A few ideas:
- default view: have the clock/icons block on the left and media-player/notification area on the right
- unlock view: label, input field and "Unlock" button on the left side of the screen, keypad on the right

I'd be willing to work on that if/when we settle on a design.

title: Lockscreen: Prevent loss of entered data by unwanted swipe gesture
description:
When on the go in a bumpy environment (e.g. bus), it often happens to me that my attempt to hit the next button on the pin pad is interpreted as a swipe, forcing me to repeat all entries.

Here is a video demonstrating the issue:

![repro-2025-10-12_20.28.37](/uploads/7f462017b1096507b40dbd6d6726862e/repro-2025-10-12_20.28.37.mp4)

Some ideas how this could be addressed:

- Limit swipe area, so swipes on the keypad (or some border around it) do not trigger the gesture
- Make the gesture available only when no characters have been entered
- Retain input, so in case of an unwanted swipe the user could return to the previous input
- Request confirmation whether swipe was intended

title: quicksettings: Allow to configure behavior in locked state per setting
description:
There are some issues like #1258 and I see other cases, where the user might not be satisifed with the default behavior of the quicksettings for a locked device.

For instance, allowing to toggle mobile data is allowed. As an end-user, I might want to restrict this so in a "lost or stolen" scenario the attacker would be forced to turn the device off to disconnect its data connection.

I think expectations here are too diverse to set on a common behavior for everybody. Instead, it would be great if there were some sensible defaults, but the behavior could also be configured/tweaked by the user per setting.

title: Add UAPI Configuration Files Specification Support
description:
The [UAPI Configuration Files Specification](https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/configuration_files_specification/) is a way of handling configuration files that uses overrides to determine functionality.

A distributor can put a config under `/usr/` (e.g. `/usr/share/phosh/`), override configs under another directory (e.g. `/usr/share/phosh/phosh.d/`), and a user/sysadmin can put their overrides in `/etc/` (with optionally a `/etc/phosh.d/` directory for user overrides alongside bare `/etc/` configs). This allows for a distribution to define their own config file and overrides without breaking any configuration by users.

This is commonly implemented using [libeconf](https://github.com/openSUSE/libeconf) to prevent duplicating config logic.

This is already partially implemented with some configs being modified with their `/etc/` counterparts, so this feature would be mostly just adding a `/usr/share/phosh/phosh.d/` directory.

title: order apps in app switcher by recently used rather than by order of being opened

Phosh gives you a list of apps from first opened to last opened with no concern for when you last used the apps.

I propose that phosh order the apps in the app switcher based on recency of use rather than on order of being opened.

title: Show both suspend and poweroff in power-menu
description:
Currently, the power and suspend buttons are in a `Gtk.Stack` and only one or the other can be displayed.

When the session is unlocked, users should be able to choose to either suspend or power off their device from the power-menu.

When the session is locked, both options should be visible (to keep the power menu consistent everywhere), but the power-off button should be disabled (until #414 is resolved). This is already the behaviour today, just stating it for completeness.

This is kinda related to #1164. What I'm driving at here is to have the power menu be consistent across unlocked sessions, locked sessions, and phrog "greeter" sessions.
